questions.prompt: A session runs in workspace-write mode with workspace /home/ana/app. A command reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and sends it to a web server. What does the mode stop?
options: Both the read and the web request
Neither, because a mode only limits writing
questions.explanation: Modes only name where a process may write. Reading and the network are outside what a mode controls, in every mode.

questions.prompt: Why does mayWrite call realpath before comparing the path with the write roots?
options: So a link inside the workspace that points elsewhere cannot carry a write out of the write roots
Because write roots are stored as links
To create the folder if it is missing
questions.explanation: A link such as app/keys -> ~/.ssh looks like it is inside the workspace. Following it first shows where the write would really land.

questions.prompt: A session switches to read-only, then stops and is resumed the next day. Which mode does it have?
options: read-only, because the switch is an event in the record
The deployment default, because modes are not saved
danger-full-access, because a resumed session starts open
No mode until a person picks one
questions.explanation: The switch is written as a sandbox/mode event. The policy reads the session's last such event, so the resumed session gets the same mode.
